attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, listed among his 'dark predictions' for GPT-4.

semantics.note: 'May' hedges only whether guardrails exist. 'Will teeter' firmly predicts both failure modes. The normalised claim keeps both modes and the qualifier.

contract.note: Reading 'teeter' as both failure modes existing together is ordinary and fair. Requiring an oscillation over time would stretch his words. There is no rate threshold, and the claim is limited to GPT-4 itself. The result depends on this reading, which the contract flags.

evidence.note: OpenAI's launch disclosure, dated 2023-03-14, shows GPT-4 shipped with safeguards. It also admits jailbreaks still exist. As a company statement about itself, it mainly establishes the condition.

Primary study (v1 May 2023) finds adversarial jailbreak prompts succeed against GPT-4 at a high rate on its selected tests. That shows the 'too weak' mode, although GPT-4 resisted better than GPT-3.5.

Peer-reviewed XSTest (responses collected 2023) shows GPT-4 refusing some harmless prompts, such as fictional-character privacy questions. That shows the 'too strong' mode, though the refusals are limited to a few prompt types.

reviews.rationale: The claim is a firm forecast with no deadline. Under the contract's early-resolution rule, dated 2023 evidence establishes both failure modes in released, safeguarded GPT-4: successful jailbreaks (e2) and refusals of harmless requests (e3). Improvement over GPT-3.5 and the localised refusals limit how severe the problem was, but neither removes a failure mode. Nothing shows the guardrails swinging back and forth over time; the contract reasonably does not require that.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Will totally eclipse' and 'safe bet' express high confidence, so this is a scored forecast. The normalisation drops 'totally' but keeps the core claim and the 'when it comes out' condition.

contract.note: Reading 'eclipse' as greater public attention than ChatGPT's launch follows from his next clause and is fair. He named no metric or time window, and GPT-4 shipped inside ChatGPT, so the result depends on comparable attention measures.

evidence.note: OpenAI release notes show GPT-4 reached ChatGPT Plus on 2023-03-14, so the release condition is met. The note says nothing about attention.
A February 2023 Google Trends analysis shows heavy attention to ChatGPT before GPT-4 launched. It makes no comparison with GPT-4's launch.

reviews.rationale: GPT-4 was released, so the condition is met. But the packet has no comparable measurement of attention to the GPT-4 launch against ChatGPT's introduction. The packet itself says no such source was found. Without that comparison, the evidence neither supports nor contradicts the forecast.
